answer: The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the ember funding graph is rebuilt from the ripple history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 282 bonds yet holds one position, and the hollow report publishes the merged exposure. Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 282 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
